answer: One concrete Sybil defense is a stakeholder bond with slashing: before an agent may attest it must lock real value, and duplicate or dishonest attestations destroy that bond. To forge a thousand fake identities, an attacker must fund a thousand separate bonds, so the cost grows linearly with the size of the farm. Validators can spot a planted orchard of look-alike agents sharing timing and funding and prune them, while the public ledger stays crystal clear about who actually paid. Making exit costly means a large fake army is far more expensive than anything it could steal.
